name: Uranus
lede: A pale cyan world tipped nearly on its side — extreme seasons and faint dark rings.

landmark.label: Equator · ring plane
landmark.blurb: Uranus rolls on its side: the equator and faint rings are nearly perpendicular to the orbital plane.

missions.name: Voyager 2
missions.note: Only spacecraft flyby — imaged rings, moons, and a nearly featureless disk at the time.

researchNotes: Uranus is an ice giant: water, ammonia, and methane ices over a rocky core, with hydrogen–helium atmosphere. Methane absorbs red light, giving the cyan hue.
Obliquity near 98° means each pole gets decades of continuous sunlight, then decades of night, across the 84-year orbit.
Faint rings and a suite of icy moons (Miranda, Ariel, Titania, Oberon, Umbriel) were revealed or refined by Voyager 2.
folklore: Named for the Greek sky god Ouranos — unusual among planets for using a Greek rather than Roman name in English.
carlFocus: Stress the tipped axis, ice-giant composition, Voyager 2 as the only flyby, and faint rings — not a second Neptune twin.
